# PRT062 `gfortran-random-extension`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="info" text="opt-in" />

The extensions `rand`, `srand`, `irand` generate random numbers.

## Why

`rand`/`srand`/`irand` are GNU extensions with a poor generator. The standard `random_number` and
`random_seed` (or `random_init`, Fortran 2018) are portable.

## Reported

```fortran
x = rand()
```

## Preferred

```fortran
call random_number(x)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[PRT062] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = PRT062` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `PORT062` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
